blocks.name: Covalent Bonds in Polymers
blocks.definition: state the role of covalent bonds in joining smaller molecules together to form polymers

blocks.md:
- A **covalent bond** is the **sharing **of two or more electrons between two atoms

  - The electrons can be shared **equally **forming a **nonpolar **covalent bond or **unequally **(where an atom can be more *electronegative* δ<sup>-</sup>) to form a **polar** covalent bond
- Generally, each atom will form a certain number of covalent bonds due to the number of free electrons in the outer orbital e.g. H = 1 bond, C = 4 bonds
- Covalent bonds are very **stable **as high energies are required to break the bonds
- Multiple pairs of electrons can be shared forming **double** bonds (e.g. unsaturated fats C=C) or **triple **bonds

blocks.alt: Diagram showing electrons shared in single and double bonds. Includes outer orbital and labels: hydrogen single bond, carbon double bond.
blocks.caption: Different types of covalent bonds

blocks.md:
- When two monomers are close enough that their outer orbitals overlap this results in their electrons being shared and a covalent bond forming

  - If more monomers are added then *polymerisation* occurs (and a polymer forms)
- A **condensation reaction** occurs when **monomers** combine together by **covalent bonds** to form **polymers** (polymerisation) or macromolecules (lipids) and **water** is **removed**

blocks.alt: Diagram of polymerisation showing removal of water molecules. Monomers combine to form a polymer, releasing water. Symbolic and written representations included.
blocks.caption: Written and symbolic illustrations of the removal of water to form a covalent bond between two or more monomers during a condensation reaction

blocks.md:
- Hydrolysis means ‘*lyse*’ (to break) and ‘*hydro*’ (with water)
- In the hydrolysis of polymers, **covalent bonds** are **broken** when **water** is **added**

blocks.alt: Diagram showing polymer hydrolysis. Water added to polymer creates monomers. Symbols: triangle monomers linked by H2O addition, forming individual units.
blocks.caption: Written and symbolic illustrations of the addition of water to break down covalent bond/s during a hydrolysis reaction
